input.prompt:
Topic: CSCI-142: Computer Science II. Create a representative course-foundations companion aligned to the official catalog description. It must teach durable concepts and problem-solving methods without claiming to replace the instructor's syllabus. Official catalog description: This course delves further into problem solving by continuing the discussion of data structure use and design, but now from an object- oriented perspective. Key topics include more information on tree and graph structures, nested data structures, objects, classes, inheritance, interfaces, object-oriented collection class libraries for abstract data types (e.g. stacks, queues, maps, and trees), and static vs. dynamic data types. Concepts of object-oriented design are a large part of the course. Software qualities related to object orientation, namely cohesion, minimal coupling, modifiability, and extensibility, are all introduced in this course, as well as a few elementary object-oriented design patterns. Input and output streams, graphical user interfaces, and exception handling are covered. Students will also be introduced to a modern integrated software development environment (IDE). Programming projects will be required. Prerequisites: CSCI-141 with a grade of C- or better or equivalent course. Contact Hours: Lecture/Lab 6 It may be used to fulfill one of the following: GE: Elective, GE: Mathematical Perspective, NTID Math Processes, SMTL: Science/Math Literacy Typically Offered: Fall, Spring, Summer

Source excerpts:

[acm-code-of-ethics]
The ACM Code directs computing professionals to contribute to society and human well-being. Computing professionals should avoid harm. They should be honest and trustworthy. They should be fair and take action not to discriminate. They should respect the work required to produce new ideas and creative works. They should respect privacy. They should honor confidentiality. Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Robust security should be designed and implemented when appropriate. Ethical computing decisions identify stakeholders, foreseeable benefits and harms, uncertainty, alternatives, and obligations.

[acm-research-practice]
Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence. It cites prior work and identifies the contribution being reported. Methods should be described well enough for readers to evaluate the work. Results should be reported accurately rather than selected to create a misleading conclusion. Limitations and threats to validity should be made visible. Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification. Conflicts and relevant relationships should be disclosed according to publication policy. A research project narrows a question, reviews literature, defines a reproducible method, evaluates results, and communicates for the intended audience.

[rit-csci-142]

Key topics include more information on tree and graph structures, nested data structures, objects, classes, inheritance, interfaces, object-oriented collection class libraries for abstract data types (e.g. stacks, queues, maps, and trees), and static vs. dynamic data types. Concepts of object-oriented design are a large part of the course. Software qualities related to object orientation, namely cohesion, minimal coupling, modifiability, and extensibility, are all introduced in this course, as well as a few elementary object-oriented design patterns. Input and output streams, graphical user interfaces, and exception handling are covered. Students will also be introduced to a modern integrated software development environment (IDE). Programming projects will be required. Prerequisites: CSCI-141 with a grade of C- or better or equivalent course. beats.claim: CSCI-142 builds on CSCI-141 by advancing problem-solving through object-oriented design, while requiring professionals to uphold ethical standards like honesty and respect for work
beats.example: Students will review the ACM Code of Ethics to understand how computing professionals must avoid harm and maintain high professional competence
beats.title: Course Scope and Ethical Practice
beats.visualDirection: Display a split-screen graphic: left side shows the ACM Code of Ethics excerpt, right side shows a checklist of ethical decision-making steps

beats.claim: Effective technical communication in computer science requires distinguishing claims from evidence and citing prior work to maintain research integrity
beats.example: Instructor will demonstrate how to structure a lab report that clearly separates observed results from theoretical claims, ensuring reproducibility
beats.title: Responsible Technical Communication
beats.visualDirection: Show a before-and-after comparison of a paragraph: first version lacks citations and conflates evidence with claims, second version uses proper attribution and clear separation

beats.claim: Object-oriented programming distinguishes static data types, which are resolved at compile time, from dynamic data types, which are resolved at runtime
beats.example: A variable declared as int in Java is static and checked during compilation, whereas a variable assigned a new object reference at runtime is dynamic
beats.title: Static vs. Dynamic Data Types
beats.visualDirection: Create a flowchart showing compile-time type checking for static types versus runtime type resolution for dynamic types, with labeled nodes

beats.claim: Classes serve as blueprints for creating objects, encapsulating data and behavior to promote modifiability and maintainability
beats.example: A class named BankAccount defines fields like balance and methods like deposit, which are instantiated into separate BankAccount objects
beats.title: Objects and Classes as Blueprints
beats.visualDirection: Render a UML class diagram showing a BankAccount class with fields and methods, alongside three instantiated object diagrams

beats.claim: Inheritance allows subclasses to inherit attributes and methods from parent classes, reducing redundancy and enhancing modifiability
beats.example: A Vehicle class defines speed and color, while a Car class inherits these properties and adds a method for honking
beats.title: Inheritance for Code Reuse
beats.visualDirection: Draw a hierarchical inheritance diagram with Vehicle at the root and Car, Truck, and Bicycle as child nodes, connected by solid lines

beats.claim: Interfaces define a set of methods that classes must implement, enabling minimal coupling and flexible extensibility across unrelated classes
beats.example: A PaymentProcessor interface requires implement classes like CreditCard and PayPal to provide a processPayment method
beats.title: Interfaces for Contractual Design
beats.visualDirection: Show a diagram of a PaymentProcessor interface with dashed arrows pointing to CreditCard and PayPal classes, labeled as implementations

beats.claim: Object-oriented collection class libraries provide abstract data types like stacks, queues, maps, and trees, enabling efficient data management
beats.example: A Stack class supports push and pop operations, while a Map class stores key-value pairs for fast retrieval
beats.title: Object-Oriented Collections and ADTs
beats.visualDirection: Display four icons representing Stack, Queue, Map, and Tree structures, each with a brief label and a small code snippet showing usage

beats.claim: High cohesion groups related data and behavior within a class, while minimal coupling reduces dependencies between classes to improve modifiability
beats.example: A GraphicsManager class handles rendering tasks, while a InputHandler class manages user events, keeping responsibilities separate
beats.title: Software Qualities: Cohesion and Minimal Coupling
beats.visualDirection: Create a block diagram showing two separate modules with clear boundaries, labeled with cohesion and coupling metrics

beats.claim: Exception handling allows programs to manage errors gracefully, while input and output streams enable data exchange with external systems
beats.example: A try-catch block catches a FileNotFoundException, and a BufferedReader reads lines from a text file into memory
beats.title: Exception Handling and I/O Streams
beats.visualDirection: Show a control flow diagram with a try block, catch block, and finally block, alongside a stream diagram showing data flow from file to program

beats.claim: Modern integrated software development environments provide tools for coding, debugging, and testing, supporting extensibility and professional practice
beats.example: Students will use an IDE to compile code, run unit tests, and view error messages, aligning with ethical and reproducible development practices
beats.title: IDE Integration and Project Workflow
beats.visualDirection: Display a screenshot of an IDE interface with highlighted regions for code editor, debugger, and terminal, annotated with workflow steps

learningObjectives: Define and distinguish between static and dynamic data types in object-oriented programming.
Explain how inheritance and interfaces enable code reuse and modifiability in software design.
Apply cohesion and minimal coupling principles to structure object-oriented collections and handle exceptions.
